clue.text: Retreat from area by marsh ground

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so its letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws from a boggy area, pulling back across soggy marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places the rearranged letters next to the abbreviation. 'Retreat' looks like a verb in the surface but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious hermitage, a secluded community where people go for spiritual withdrawal and contemplation.

clue.text: Soprano singer, one covering last of jazz pieces

indicators.note: a covering sits right against what it covers, so two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: S is the musical abbreviation for soprano
Cher is the famous American pop singer

indicators.note: the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soprano and a fellow singer perform, one of them covering the closing numbers of a jazz set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' is the definition: SCHERZI is the plural of scherzo, a lively movement in a symphony or sonata.
explanation.definitionFit: Scherzi are musical movements or compositions, so they are pieces of music in the plural, matching the plural definition.

clue.text: Lying Conservative in Number Ten endlessly partying

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other
people partying are wild and all over the place, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the word loses its last letter
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A dishonest Tory in Downing Street keeps holding parties, a jab at lockdown-era scandals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths, but it means lying down. Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence; here the words simply supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes a body reclining or stretched out horizontally, which is the positional sense of lying rather than deceiving.

clue.text: Stupid to roll over stone in centre

indicators.note: rolling over turns a thing upside down, and in a down entry that flips the order of its letters

parts.note: dim means slow-witted
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Some dimwit is told to roll over a stone sitting in the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word joining wordplay to the definition 'centre'.
explanation.definitionFit: The midst of something is its middle or central part, as in 'in the midst of the crowd'.

clue.text: Fried food with chilli one's put onto greens?

parts.note: chips are fried potatoes, British for fries
food with chilli is spicy, or hot

explanation.surface: Chips topped with chilli, served on a bed of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' looks like salad vegetables but means golf greens; 'put' also hints at a golf putt. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a chip shot is a short lofted stroke played from near the green, meant to land the ball on the putting surface.

clue.text: Conservative Party Conference, say, with stars

parts.note: a party conference is an example of a convention
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: The Conservative Party Conference, attended by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' seems to name the political party, but it is the definition with a small c: someone who sticks to tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A conventionalist follows established customs and resists change, which is the general, non-political sense of a conservative person.

clue.text: Determined relative maybe camping outside

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: someone camping is in a tent
a sister is one example of a relative; 'maybe' marks the example

explanation.surface: A resolute family member insists on camping out rather than staying indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camping' has to be read as the two words 'in tent', which then open up to take the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insistent keeps demanding something firmly and will not give up, so they are resolute and determined.

clue.text: Like a judge in his garb, swapping sides

indicators.note: trading sides means the letters at each end change places with each other

parts.note: a judge's garb is his robes

explanation.surface: A judge sitting in his robes, perhaps changing allegiance in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'sober as a judge'. Exchanging the first and last letters of the garment word gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase 'sober as a judge' makes a judge the proverbial example of someone completely serious and clear-headed.

clue.text: Mostly leave out nuts to make eggs

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to skip most of the nuts when baking with eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like an ingredient to leave out of a recipe, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To ovulate is to release an egg from the ovary, so the verb means producing eggs biologically.

clue.text: Hatchling hiding tail with it

indicators.note: with its tail hidden away, the final letter is no longer visible

parts.note: a newly hatched bird is a chick

explanation.surface: A newly hatched bird tucks its tail away as it goes along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like a joining phrase but is the definition, an old slang for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'with it' means stylish and up to date, and chic describes elegant, fashionable style.

clue.text: What diner orders contains an off-colour dairy product

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a diner orders a dish
taken as written
off-colour jokes are risqué, or blue

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer's order includes some dairy that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-colour' suggests food turned mouldy, but it means smutty. Danish blue is a strong blue-veined cheese from Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish blue is a cheese, and cheese is made from milk, so it is a dairy product.

clue.text: Thief who was bound for America swallows two drugs

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece takes others into itself

parts.note: pro means in favour of
US is the abbreviation for the United States
METH (methamphetamine) and E (ecstasy) are two drug abbreviations

explanation.surface: A criminal being transported to America gulps down drugs to smuggle them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound for America' reads as travelling there, but 'bound' belongs to the definition: Prometheus was chained to a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Prometheus stole fire from the gods and was punished by being chained to a rock, so he is a thief who was bound.

clue.text: What sleeper does naked in sheets

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a sleeper dreams

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps in the nude between the bedsheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheets' looks like bedding, but it means sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper, traditionally five hundred sheets, so it stands for a stack of sheets.

clue.text: Way to get lift to conserve energy using complex engineering

indicators.note: conserving something means keeping it safe inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: hitching a ride is a way to get a lift
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An engineer's plan for generating lift while saving energy through clever design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' sounds like aerodynamics, but it is a ride, as in hitchhiking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes things built with advanced technology and sophisticated machinery, which is what using complex engineering means.

clue.text: Give cook sandwiches recipe? Rolls will contain this!

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it

indicators.note: a sandwich has its filling held between slices, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to bake is to cook
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'take'

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to make sandwiches, with bread rolls holding the filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like bread rolls but means a car rolling, or a Rolls-Royce; the exclamation mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbrake holds a parked vehicle still, so it restrains, or contains, a car's rolling motion, including a Rolls-Royce.

clue.text: One still growing green tea abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters are sent off into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A plant still growing is green tea cultivated overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One still growing' suggests a tea plant, but it describes a young person who has not finished growing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is an adolescent aged thirteen to nineteen, still physically developing and not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Bard's killer guardian clutching a spear?

parts.note: in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, Cleopatra dies by the bite of an asp

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip tightly within one's grasp, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Argus was the hundred-eyed watchman of Greek myth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's murderer is a guard holding a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bard's killer' suggests someone who killed Shakespeare, but it means a killer in his plays. 'Spear' is a single stalk of the vegetable, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus shoots are called spears, so a spear is an example of the vegetable, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Console popular nurse beset by rejection

indicators.note: being beset means being surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: no is a refusal
what is popular is in
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Comforting a well-liked nurse who has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like a verb meaning comfort, but it is a noun: a games console.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is a Japanese company that makes video game consoles such as the Switch, so the brand stands for a games machine.

clue.text: Chain encircling turned-up collar shows decorative art

indicators.note: to encircle is to ring something round, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: Ikea is the Swedish furniture store chain

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means flipped to read bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to nab them

explanation.surface: A necklace worn around a turned-up shirt collar is a decorative flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain' and 'collar' suggest jewellery and clothing; the first is a shop chain and the second means arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging, a decorative art form practised for centuries.

clue.text: Aristo saving tiny bit of cash shows intelligence

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safe inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class person
1p, one penny, read as the letters I and P

explanation.surface: A wealthy aristocrat who hoards every penny proves to be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny is written 1p, and the 1 is read as the letter I. 'Intelligence' means information, as in military intelligence, not brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a piece of secret information or a warning, which is intelligence in the sense of gathered information.

clue.text: Suit jackets pale, worn in dingy cinema

indicators.note: a jacket wraps around what it covers, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to suit is to fit

indicators.note: worn means battered out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Faded suit jackets worn by people sitting in a shabby picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit jackets' reads as clothing, but 'suit' is a verb and 'jackets' is the wrapping signal. A fleapit is British slang for a run-down cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleapit is informal British slang for a shabby old cinema or theatre, jokingly suggesting it is infested with fleas.

clue.text: Man associated with Nazis?

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A question about some man linked with the Nazi regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a male pronoun joined to the Nazi SS gives a leading Nazi.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy in the Nazi party, famous for his solo flight to Scotland in 1941.

clue.text: Theresa unabashed to strip off in steamy location

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer layers, leaving only the letters in the middle of the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A shameless woman named Theresa undresses somewhere hot and steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures undressing, but stripping off here removes the outer letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a room heated with steam or dry heat for bathing and relaxing, so it is a steamy place.

clue.text: Gamble, investing reserve when selling's advised

indicators.note: to invest can mean to clothe or surround, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
to earmark funds is to reserve them

explanation.surface: A stock market tip: take a gamble with your reserve funds when it is time to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' fits the financial surface, but here it means wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear market is a period of falling share prices, when investors expect declines and are inclined to sell.

clue.text: What Angus has to say about abstemious gnome

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: an Aberdeen Angus is a breed of cattle, and cattle say moo
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A Scotsman named Angus talks about a garden gnome that never drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Angus looks like a Scottish man's name, but it is the cattle breed. 'Gnome' means a short saying, not a garden ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in its rarer sense is a pithy maxim or aphorism, and a motto is a short saying expressing a principle.

clue.text: Attenborough, say, is one revealing all about animal's skin

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a naturist is a nudist, who reveals everything

indicators.note: the skin is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A wildlife broadcaster tells all about an animal's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing all' sounds like a documentary exposé, but it describes a nudist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir David Attenborough is the famous British wildlife broadcaster, an example of someone who studies nature; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Opening with Mahler's Fifth generates yawn

parts.note: an opening is a gap

indicators.note: the fifth of a word is its fifth letter, so just that one letter is kept

parts.note: the fifth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Starting a concert with Mahler's Fifth Symphony sends the audience to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mahler's Fifth' looks like the symphony, but it is the fifth letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, and a yawn is exactly that involuntary wide opening.

clue.text: Colourful chatterer's caress entertaining a debauchee

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in your home, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: to pet is to stroke or caress
taken as written
a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeking man

explanation.surface: A flamboyant smooth-talker fondles a libertine he is entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful chatterer' reads as a vivid gossip, but it is a bright talking bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small, brightly plumaged parrot, and parrots are known for their noisy chatter and mimicry.

clue.text: About to park behind European at that place

indicators.note: behind means immediately next to in a line, so two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: on means about, concerning
to park oneself is to sit down
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone is about to park behind a European car at a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' suggests a car, but it means to sit down, as in 'park yourself'.
explanation.definitionFit: On-site means at the location in question, such as work carried out at the place itself rather than elsewhere.
